quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When stopping at an intersection with a stop line, where should you stop?

options.text: After the stop line.
At the stop line.
In the crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: At the stop line.
questions.explanation: A stop line is a white line painted across the road at intersections. You must stop at the stop line when a pedestrian is present or when a sign or signal tells you to stop.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with care.
Continue normally through the intersection.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Stop and proceed when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with care.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means "caution." When you see this light, slow down, look both ways, and proceed carefully.

questions.question: What does a broken white line on a highway mean?

options.text: You cannot cross the line to pass.
You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
You may only cross the line to change lanes if you are in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
questions.explanation: White dashed lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross a dashed white line to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Drive at the same speed.
Slow down to give them room to pass safely.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give them room to pass safely.
questions.explanation: Slow down when someone wants to pass you. This creates space in front of your vehicle so they can complete the pass quickly and easily.

questions.question: What is the penalty for not securing child passengers in a safety belt or car seat?

options.text: A fine and one point on your driving record.
Two points on your driving record.
Two points and court costs.

questions.correctAnswerText: A fine and one point on your driving record.
questions.explanation: Children under 18 must be secured in a safety belt or car seat. A violation results in a fine of $25 (plus court costs) and one point on your driving record.

questions.question: When a green light changes to yellow as you approach an intersection, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get through the light.
Brake hard to stop immediately.
Be ready to stop in the middle of the intersection.
Be ready to stop before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop before the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light warns you that the light will turn red soon. Prepare to stop safely before entering the intersection.

questions.question: The amount of alcohol in the blood is called:

options.text: Implied consent (IC).
Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).

questions.correctAnswerText: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in your blood. A higher BAC means greater impairment.

questions.question: If you have a green light but traffic is blocking the intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Turn left and find another route.
Wait outside the intersection until traffic clears.
Follow other vehicles into the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait outside the intersection until traffic clears.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, do not enter the intersection if traffic is blocking your path. Entering when the light turns red will block cross traffic and you can receive a ticket.

questions.question: How must all children under age 18 ride in a vehicle?

options.text: In the back seat.
In the front seat.
Secured in a safety belt or car seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secured in a safety belt or car seat.
questions.explanation: Children under 18 must be secured with a safety belt or car seat when riding in a moving vehicle.

questions.question: When you see vehicles on an interstate entrance ramp to your right, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to block their entry.
Stay in your lane.
Move left to give them space to enter safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move left to give them space to enter safely.
questions.explanation: Signal and move left to allow vehicles from the entrance ramp room to merge safely. If moving left is unsafe, slow down to help them merge.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Change lanes suddenly without warning.
Check for other vehicles in the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes suddenly without warning.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and blind spots to make sure no vehicles are there. Always use your turn signal before changing lanes. This gives other drivers time to react.

questions.question: When driving past a parked car on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Expect the driver to open the car door as you pass.
Speed up.
Brake hard.
Expect the driver to wait until you pass before opening the door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the driver to open the car door as you pass.
questions.explanation: When passing a parked car, be prepared for the driver to open the door. Use extra caution when driving near parked vehicles.

questions.question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night, you should:

options.text: Look toward the right edge of the road.
Switch your lights to high beams.
Turn your lights on and off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights blind you, look toward the right edge of the road instead of straight ahead. This keeps your car safe on the road until you pass the other vehicle.

questions.question: Drivers may pass on a two-lane road with a solid yellow line on their side of the center.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You can only pass when the broken yellow line is on your side. A solid yellow line on your side means you cannot pass.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Signal before going further.
Slow down and yield to trains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield to trains.
questions.explanation: This round sign warns you of a railroad crossing ahead. Slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop for trains.

questions.question: It is against the law to drive a vehicle with a television screen visible to the driver.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: It is illegal to operate a vehicle with a television screen that the driver can see.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: One-way traffic.
Divided highway ahead.
Two-way traffic.
Keep left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black text on a yellow background. They alert you to hazards. This sign warns you that a divided highway is ahead.

questions.question: If a bus is signaling to return to the road after a stop, you must:

options.text: Honk to let them know you are there.
Move to the left lane.
Yield.
Speed up to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield.
questions.explanation: You must yield to a bus returning to the road after stopping. Slow down, change lanes, or stop to let the bus safely enter traffic.

questions.question: When turning left, drivers must yield to:

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.
Oncoming traffic.
Pedestrians already in the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic, pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.question: You need extra caution driving near a pedestrian with a white cane because:

options.text: They are deaf.
They are a police officer.
They are blind.
They have poor balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are blind.
questions.explanation: A white cane means the pedestrian is blind. Slow down, yield the right-of-way, and be ready to stop to prevent injury.

questions.question: Which of these is unlawful?

options.text: Pass a school bus with flashing red lights and a stop arm extended.
Pass within 100 feet of an intersection.
Pass within 100 feet of a railroad crossing.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: It is unlawful to pass in many situations. You cannot pass a school bus loading or unloading children. You also cannot pass within 100 feet of a railroad crossing, within 100 feet of an intersection, or in any no passing zone.

questions.question: When must you show proof of insurance to a police officer?

options.text: Only if you are in a collision.
If you are in a collision or stopped for a traffic ticket.
Only if you are stopped and given a ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are in a collision or stopped for a traffic ticket.
questions.explanation: You must carry proof of insurance whenever you drive. You must show your proof of insurance and driver's license to a police officer whenever you are stopped or involved in a collision.

questions.question: What should you do if you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead?

options.text: Keep going. You have the right-of-way.
Wait for the pedestrians to finish crossing.
Turn right and drive around the pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrians to finish crossing.
questions.explanation: You must let pedestrians cross in a crosswalk. Wait until the intersection is clear before you drive forward.

questions.question: On a freeway, why should you look farther ahead than on a city street?

options.text: To spot hazards early.
Because your car needs a quarter mile to stop.
To keep up with traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: To spot hazards early.
questions.explanation: On the freeway, watch for changes in traffic conditions and signals from other drivers. Be ready for vehicles merging at on-ramps and expect rapid changes in road conditions.

questions.question: What does a green arrow on a lane control signal mean?

options.text: You may use this lane.
No traffic is allowed in this lane.
You have the right-of-way.
You must move into this lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may use this lane.
questions.explanation: A green arrow pointing down on a lane means you can use that lane.
